Die Teams arbeiten eigenständig, werden aber angeleitet. Teilnehmende arbeiten hands-on mit Clouddiensten und Open-Source-Software. Teilweise sind Projekte in Kooperation mit externen Partnern. Details werden zu Beginn des Semesters bekanntgegeben.
course_summary: Hands-on, project-based course where small student teams design, implement, and prototype real distributed-system applications (cloud, fog, web, IoT). Students use cloud services, modern software stacks and open-source tools to solve practical challenges, run full software-development lifecycles, and work with or coordinate external partners. Emphasis on independent teamwork, practical engineering skills, and identifying and communicating open research questions. Terms offered: fall and spring semesters (availability may vary by institution).

title: Eventbasierte Maschinelles Sehen
learn_outcomes: Participants will learn basic concepts, theoretical foundations and relevant algorithms developed in the field of event-based (i.e., neuromorphic) vision. Upon completing the module, participants will have an overview of the field, spanning from the principle of operation of event-based sensors (e.g., event-based cameras), their advantages and disadvantages, to the methods used to process their output for a target application. Participants will also be aware of the differences with standard (frame-based) computer vision, in terms of methods, performance criteria and applications.
learn_content:
This course is the first of its kind, worldwide. To the best of the instructor's knowledge, no similar course has been offered anywhere due to the novelty of the topics covered, which have appeared in research conferences and journals over the last ten years.

The topics covered include the following:
Bio-inspired principle of operation of event-based (i.e., neuromorphic) sensors.
Event-based feature detection and tracking.
Event-based motion estimation: optical flow estimation, 3D reconstruction, camera localization and ego-motion estimation, simultaneous localization and mapping (E-SLAM).
Stereo depth estimation in dynamic scenes.
Image intensity reconstruction from events.
Event-based pattern recognition, classification and machine learning.
Event-based signal processing and filtering.
Event-based sensor fusion.
Event-based control.
Event-based (i.e., spike-based) hardware.
Novel applications in event-based vision.
course_summary: This course introduces event-based (neuromorphic) vision: operation principles of event-based sensors, their pros/cons vs. frame-based cameras, and algorithms to process event streams. Topics include feature detection and tracking, optical flow, 3D reconstruction, ego-motion and E‑SLAM, stereo depth in dynamic scenes, image intensity reconstruction, event-based pattern recognition and machine learning, signal processing and filtering, sensor fusion, event-based control, spike-based hardware, and novel applications. Students will understand both theoretical foundations and practical methods for applying event-driven vision in robotics, perception, and embedded systems.

title: Fairness, Rechenschaftspflicht und Transparenz beim maschinellen Lernen
learn_outcomes:
Am Ende des Kurses werden die Studierenden in der Lage sein:

 - Unterschiedliche Narrative und Konzepte rund um Machine Learning / KI zu erklären und zu verstehen, wie sie aktuelle Forschungsrichtungen und Implementierungen beeinflussen.
 - Situationen und soziotechnische Systeme zu identifizieren, in denen automatisierte Entscheidungsfindung legitim ist und wo nicht.
 - Wichtige Metriken zu Fairness und Bias sowie Strategien zur Bias-Minderung in der algorithmischen Entscheidungsfindung und NLP zu diskutieren und anzuwenden, einschließlich der Erklärung des Fairness-Unmöglichkeitstheorems.
 - Transparenzmaßnahmen wie Modell- und Dokumentationsmethoden für Daten zu verstehen und Transparenztechniken wie interpretierbare ML-Methoden anzuwenden, um Entscheidungsprozesse von Modellen und NLP zu analysieren.
 - Konzepte der Verantwortlichkeit zu erklären und aktuelle Bemühungen in der EU zur Regulierung von KI / ML zu benennen.
 - Konzepte von FAccT-ML anzuwenden, um soziotechnische Systeme zu analysieren und zu bewerten und Audit-Studien durchführen zu können.
learn_content:
Maschinelle Lernsysteme (ML) und Systeme für algorithmische Entscheidungsfindung (ADM) werden in immer mehr Kontexten eingesetzt. Diese Systeme filtern, sortieren, empfehlen und personalisieren Inhalte/Daten. Sie werden zunehmend auch in Entscheidungsprozessen verwendet, die erhebliche Auswirkungen auf das Leben von Individuen und somit auf die Gesellschaft haben, wie etwa beim Zugang zu Krediten, Versicherungen, Gesundheitsversorgung, Bewährung und Einwanderung.

Dieser Kurs konzentriert sich auf die informatischen und sozialen Perspektiven sowie Methoden zur Analyse und Bewertung von automatisierter Entscheidungsfindung und ML-Systemen und deren Auswirkungen. Zu den im Kurs behandelten Konzepten zählen Biases und Fairness, Transparenzmaßnahmen wie Erklärbarkeit, Interpretierbarkeit und Dokumentation von ML-Systemen sowie die Bewertung und Auditierung solcher Systeme.

Zusammengefasst werden im Kurs folgende Themen behandelt:

 - Überblick über das Feld „Fairness, Verantwortlichkeit und Transparenz (FAccT) im Maschinellen Lernen“
 - Narrative rund um maschinelles Lernen, soziotechnische Systeme und die Legitimität automatisierter Entscheidungsfindung
 - Begriffe von Fairness, Bias und Fairness-Metriken sowie Methoden zur Bias-Minderung
 - Fairness und NLP
 - Transparenz (Erklärbarkeit, Interpretierbarkeit, Dokumentation etc.)
 - Interpretierbarkeit und NLP
 - Verantwortlichkeit (Verantwortungen, Audit-Studien, EU-Regulierung, Lieferkette für ML)
course_summary: This course introduces the field of Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT) in machine learning. Students learn to analyze narratives and sociotechnical contexts that shape ML/AI systems, assess where automated decision-making is (in)appropriate, and perform sociotechnical analyses of ML deployments. The course covers fairness concepts and bias, fairness metrics (including the impossibility theorem), bias-mitigation strategies, and specific issues for NLP. It also teaches transparency techniques—explainability, interpretability, data/model documentation—and accountability topics such as audits, responsibilities across the ML supply chain, and current EU regulatory efforts. By course end students can apply FAccT methods to evaluate, document, and audit algorithmic decision systems.

title: Modulbeschreibung ohne Titel
learn_outcomes: Students have an in-depth understanding of selected early vision models of human perception and their implementation in hardware (neuromorphic cameras). They are able to present and convey the acquired knowledge and skills eloquently.
learn_content: The project topic is subject to change, and will be made available before the start of each semester. Please see: http://www.psyco.tu-berlin.de/teaching.html
course_summary: Project-based course focused on selected early-vision models of human perception and their implementation on neuromorphic (event-based) camera hardware. Students gain in-depth theoretical and practical knowledge of biologically inspired visual processing, work on a semester-specific project, and develop skills in presenting and communicating technical results.

title: Quantum Computing
learn_outcomes:
This course provides theoretical as well as practical introduction to quantum computation. 
By the end of the course students will be able to understand basics of quantum mechanics, quantum logic and computation, important quantum-algorithms, and work with actual quantum computers and quantum simulators.
learn_content:
List of topics covered: 

- (Just) enough quantum mechanics to understand quantum computation
- Quantum algorithms
- Simon's algorithm
- The prime factorization algorithm
- Grover's search algorithm
- Mathematical models of quantum computation, their relationships to each other, and to physical systems.
- Quantum error correcting codes

Exercises ------------------------------------------------------

- Backgrounds : The need for quantum computing
- Hardware technologies for quantum computers
- Quantum logic
- Computation on a quantum computer
- Programming on IBM Q
course_summary: Introductory course in quantum computation covering foundational quantum mechanics and quantum logic sufficient for computing, central quantum algorithms (Simon's, Shor’s prime-factorization, Grover), mathematical models of quantum computation and their relation to physical systems, and quantum error-correcting codes. Includes practical components: hardware technologies, programming and exercises on IBM Q, use of quantum simulators, and hands-on computation on real quantum devices.

title: Modulbeschreibung ohne Titel
learn_outcomes: Students acquire the fundamental background on Wireless Communication Systems and a broad overview of the current and near future standards such as LTE and 5G Wireless Networks. Furthermore, students acquire concepts and principles of the economic and market drivers beyond the development of wireless communication systems, and get ideas and examples of the industrial research and standardization process behind the development of such systems.
learn_content:
This module deals with the theoretical basis and most relevant wireless communication systems and discusses their architecture, interfaces and services. In the theoretical part the cellular concept, radio propagation and diversity, digital modulation, coding and scheduling as well as multiple access schemes are explained to derive the basic system concepts of deployed systems. The corresponding radio interfaces are explained and compared. As an example of today’s broadband mobile systems based on IP technology, LTE and 5G are presented in detail. System planning and maintenance issues are introduced as well. A special highlight consists of the economic importance and costs of the different components of the system. In an outlook future research directions towards beyond 5G / 6G systems as well as means for collaborative research are presented. It is the objective of this module to link communication theory with industrial research and development towards deployed systems in our societies and economies.

•	Basic environment of Mobile Communication: History of Mobile Communication, Market, Regulation and Standardization, Frequencies, Mobile Channel, Cellular Radio, Services.
•	Theoretical foundation of wireless communication systems including cellular concept, radio propagation and diversity, digital modulation, multiple access schemes, coding and scheduling.
•	Overview of Wireless Communication Systems: Public Cellular Mobile Radio Systems, Trunked Mobile Radio, Broadband Wireless Access (WiFi, WiMax).
•	Network Planning and Optimization.
•	GSM: General overview, Architecture, The Radio Interface, Signaling Architecture and Protocols, Signaling Functions, Network Management, GSM-R.
•	3G Systems: General overview, Architecture, The Radio Interface, HSPA, Basic Core Entities, The Core Network, Services.
•	4G and 5G: Multi Radio Access, End-to-End IP, LTE, Further research activities.
•	Economics: Basics, Structure of the Business Case UMTS, Business Case LTE, new business models for 5G for verticals.
•	Applications (WLANs, Cellular, Vectoring in cable modem transmission)
course_summary: This module provides a comprehensive introduction to wireless communication systems, combining theoretical foundations with practical, industrial and economic perspectives. It covers cellular concepts, radio propagation and diversity, digital modulation, coding, multiple access methods, and scheduling; compares radio interfaces and architectures (GSM, 3G/HSPA, LTE, 5G) and surveys broadband wireless access (Wi‑Fi, WiMax). Students learn network planning and optimization, system interfaces and core network functions, and study IP‑based end‑to‑end mobile systems. The course also examines market, regulation, standardization and the economics of mobile systems (business cases for UMTS/LTE and new 5G verticals), as well as research and outlook toward beyond‑5G/6G and collaborative R&D.

title: Ausgewählte Bereiche der Telekommunikationsnetze
learn_outcomes:
Das Hauptziel dieses Moduls besteht darin, das technische Wissen im Bereich der Kommunikationsnetze zu vertiefen. Insbesondere werden die Studierenden ein tieferes Verständnis für spezifische Technologien und deren Eigenschaften (grundlegende Funktionalität, Anpassung an Nutzeranforderungen usw.) erlangen. Sie erhalten die Möglichkeit, ihr Wissen über ausgewählte Kommunikationstechnologien (UMTS/LTE, Internet, Multimedia, Ad-hoc-, Sensornetze usw.) zu erweitern.

Darüber hinaus bietet die Lehrveranstaltung die Gelegenheit, Kenntnisse über die Schnittmengen vieler verschiedener Kommunikationstechnologien zu vertiefen, die aus unterschiedlichen Perspektiven (drahtlose Kommunikation, Hochgeschwindigkeitsnetze) behandelt werden.

In den Seminaren haben die Studierenden außerdem die Möglichkeit, eine ausgewählte Technologie oder ein technologieorientiertes Problem auszuarbeiten und dieses vor einem größeren Publikum zu präsentieren. Dies trägt sowohl zur Entwicklung praktischer Präsentationsfähigkeiten als auch zur Förderung des kritischen Denkens bei.
learn_content:
Im Seminar werden eine große Vielfalt von Themen aus dem Bereich der drahtlosen mobilen Kommunikation nach Wahl der Studierenden behandelt. In jedem Semester wird ein spezifischerer Schwerpunkt des Seminars festgelegt (z. B. Verkehrsmanagement in LTE-Netzen, energieeffiziente drahtlose Netzwerke usw.). Innerhalb dieses technischen Rahmens wird von den Studierenden erwartet, dass sie eigene Vorschläge für interessante Fragestellungen einbringen, an denen sie im Seminar arbeiten möchten.

Nach einer gemeinsamen Diskussion werden detaillierte Seminarthemen festgelegt und individuell den Studierenden zur Bearbeitung während des Semesters zugewiesen. Zu den Hauptaufgaben, die die Studierenden erfüllen sollen, gehören: die Identifizierung der wichtigsten aktuellen Forschungsarbeiten, die mit dem Seminarthema in Zusammenhang stehen, die Klassifizierung der gesammelten Forschungsartikel anhand einer gut begründeten Taxonomie, die Bestimmung der wichtigsten offenen Forschungsfragen sowie die Erarbeitung von Perspektiven für zukünftige Forschung.
course_summary: This seminar deepens technical knowledge of communication networks and selected wireless/mobile technologies (e.g., UMTS/LTE, Internet multimedia, ad-hoc and sensor networks). Students explore technology-specific functionality and trade-offs, study intersections across wireless and high-speed networks, and research a focused topic set each semester. Tasks include literature identification, taxonomy-based classification, pinpointing open research questions, and proposing future research directions; students also present their work to develop presentation and critical-thinking skills. Offered: every semester (topic/focus changes each term).

title: Eventbasierte Maschinelles Sehen - PROJEKT
learn_outcomes: Participants of this project course will gain practical experience in applying techniques from event-based and computer vision to solve problems in robot perception (motion estimation, recognition, etc.). Participants will work individually or in a small team collaboratively, and will acquire knowledge about the state-of-the-art on event-based vision related to the chosen problem.
learn_content:
Event-based vision is an emerging technology that promises to offer advantages to overcome some of the limitations of traditional, frame-based cameras and visual processing pipelines (from sensors to output, actionable information), such as latency, dynamic range, bandwidth and power consumption. To unlock the advantages of event-based cameras, new algorithms are needed to process their unconventional output (a stream of asynchronous pixel-wise intensity changes, as opposed to the familiar video images of standard cameras). This project is related to the investigation and development of tailored algorithms and methods to tackle specific problems in event-based vision (motion estimation, segmentation, object detection and recognition, etc.). 

At the beginning of the module, students receive or select project topics from a list of possible ones, as well as some introductory material related to the chosen problem. After setting the project teams and topics, the suitable tools to carry out the project are discussed and set up. The students prepare a project plan, specify the data on which they will be working on and the steps that are anticipated for a successful completion of the project. During the remaining weeks the students develop their projects and discuss the progress with the instructor, to guide future action items. At the end of the project, the students present their findings to other students in the module, with an oral presentation. They summarize not only the technical outcome of the project but also the difficulties and lessons learned during the project.

The general topics include but are not limited to:
- Algorithms: visual odometry, SLAM, 3D reconstruction, optical flow estimation, image intensity reconstruction, recognition, stereo depth reconstruction, feature/object detection, tracking, calibration, sensor fusion (video synthesis, visual-inertial odometry, etc.).
- Event camera datasets and/or simulators.
- Event-based signal processing, representation, control, bandwidth control.
- Event-based active vision, event-based sensorimotor integration.
- Applications in: robotics (navigation, manipulation, drones...), automotive, IoT, AR/VR, space science, inspection, surveillance, crowd counting, physics, biology.
- Model-based, embedded, or learning approaches.
- Novel hardware (cameras, neuromorphic processors, etc.) and/or software platforms.
- New trends and challenges in event-based and/or biologically-inspired vision (SNNs, etc.).
- Event-based vision for computational photography.
A longer list of related topics is available in the table of content of this repository: https://github.com/uzh-rpg/event-based_vision_resources/
course_summary: Project-based course on event-based (neuromorphic) vision for robot perception. Students work individually or in small teams to research, develop and evaluate tailored algorithms and systems that process asynchronous event-camera output for tasks such as motion estimation, SLAM, depth/stereo, optical flow, reconstruction, detection, recognition and sensor fusion. The module emphasizes hands-on project planning, dataset selection or simulator use, implementation (model-based, embedded or learning methods), iterative progress reviews with the instructor, and a final oral presentation reporting technical results, challenges and lessons learned. Applications span robotics, automotive, AR/VR, IoT and scientific domains, and may involve novel hardware and neuromorphic computing.

title: Cloud Service Benchmarking
learn_outcomes: Die Studierenden haben Wissen über Benchmarking (insbesondere von Clouddiensten und in der Cloud) und sind in der Lage, dieses Wissen praktisch anzuwenden. Dies beinhaltet alle Schritte von der Bedarfsanalyse zu Benchmarking, Design von Benchmark und Messmethode unter Berücksichtigung von Benchmarking-Best-Practices, die Benchmarkimplementierung, die Ausführung cloudbasierter Experimente, sowie die Analyse und Interpretation der Messergebnisse. Die Studierenden sind in der Lage die Ergebnisse schriftlich und mündlich zu kommunizieren.
learn_content: Das Modul behandelt Grundlagen sowie den gesamten Lifecycle von Benchmarking. Dies wird sowohl in Form von flipped classroom basierend auf einem Buch als auch basierend auf individuellen Benchmarkingprojekten gemacht. Weitere Informationen zu den Kursinhalten können auf der Website des Buches gefunden werden: https://cloudservicebenchmarking.github.io/
course_summary: This course teaches the full lifecycle of benchmarking cloud services, combining theory and hands-on practice. Students learn requirement analysis, benchmark and measurement design following best practices, implementation of benchmarks, execution of cloud-based experiments, and analysis and interpretation of results. Emphasis is placed on communicating findings both in writing and orally; instruction is delivered via a flipped-classroom model and individual benchmarking projects based on the referenced textbook and website.

title: Reading Group Cloud Systems
learn_outcomes: Students have an overview of state-of-the-art cloud systems. Students have gained experience in reading scientific papers. Students are able to participate in and organize scientific discussions on cloud systems.
learn_content: The course covers state-of-the-art cloud systems based on scientific papers. The actual set of papers will vary over different semesters. Typical examples of such papers would be Dynamo, Google File System, BigTable, Cassandra, MapReduce, OpenWhisk, or SAND.
course_summary: A seminar-style reading group surveying state-of-the-art cloud systems through discussion of primary research papers. Students develop familiarity with influential systems (e.g., Dynamo, GFS, BigTable, Cassandra, MapReduce, OpenWhisk, SAND), gain skills in reading and critiquing scientific literature, and learn to organize and lead technical discussions on topics such as distributed storage, consistency, scalability, fault tolerance, and serverless platforms.

title: DCAITI: Projekt Simulation Vertiefung vernetztes und automatisiertes Fahren
learn_outcomes: Die Studierenden haben mit Hilfe von Simulationen praktische Erfahrungen mit der Umsetzung und Validierung von vernetzten Mobilitätsanwendungen gesammelt. Zielsysteme sind neben den automatisierten Fahrzeugen auch Smartphones.
learn_content: Dieses Modul ist als Vertiefung zu unserer Lehrveranstaltung sim VAF zu verstehen und bietet den Studierenden die Möglichkeiten der Simulation von Anwendungen, die auf Fahrzeug-zu-X Kommunikation basieren. Beispielhafte Anwendungen betreffen verschiedene Bereiche des autonomen Fahrens, Verkehrseffizienz oder Komfort-Applikationen. Im Projekt soll unsere vorhandene Simulationsumgebung "Eclipse MOSAIC" verwendet und weiter entwickelt werden. In initialen Fachvorträgen stellen wir verschiedene Simulatoren, Tools und Ansätze vor, die innerhalb unserer Simulationsumgebung zum Einsatz kommen. Gemeinsam werden dann einzelne weiterführenden Aspekte erarbeitet, die selbstständig gelöst, implementiert, in Kurzvorträgen präsentiert und entsprechenden Dokumentation niedergeschrieben werden.
course_summary: Project-based advanced module on simulation, implementation and validation of connected and automated driving applications. Students use and extend the Eclipse MOSAIC simulation environment to model vehicle-to-X communication involving automated vehicles and smartphones. Typical use cases include autonomous driving functions, traffic-efficiency measures and comfort applications. Work includes adapting/implementing simulators and tools, developing and validating applications in simulation, presenting results in short talks and producing documentation. Offered as a project module, typically available in both winter and summer terms (check local timetable for exact offering).

title: Internet of Services Lab (Seminar)
learn_outcomes:
In diesem Kurs lernen die Teilnehmer:
(1) wie man eine Literaturrecherche durchführt und wie man Forschungsarbeiten liest und analysiert, 
(2) wie man eine gute wissenschaftliche Präsentation hält, um seine akademischen Kommunikationsfähigkeiten zu verbessern, 
(3) wie man eine Arbeit in akademischer Sprache verfasst. 

Darüber hinaus erhalten die Studierenden Expertenwissen und Einblicke in einen bestimmten Forschungsbereich.
learn_content:
Die Studierenden bearbeiten einzeln oder in kleinen Gruppen ein vorgegebenes Seminarthema unter wissenschaftlicher Betreuung. Die Studierenden nutzen die Literaturrecherche als Methodik, um Informationen aus wissenschaftlichen Informationsquellen zu sammeln und die gesammelten Informationen zu systematisieren. Auf diese Weise identifizieren die Studierenden eine Forschungslücke und formulieren offene Forschungsprobleme/-fragen. Anschließend verfassen die Studierenden zwei Versionen ihrer Arbeit [Erstversion und Endversion]. 

Zusätzlich zum Verfassen der Arbeit werden die Studierenden ihre Arbeit in einer mündlichen Präsentation zusammenfassen und ihre Ergebnisse einem akademischen Publikum vorstellen. Darüber hinaus werden die Studierenden in einer Vorlesung mit den relevanten Aspekten des wissenschaftlichen Schreibens vertraut gemacht und erfahren, wie sie eine wissenschaftliche Arbeit strukturieren können und wie der Peer-Review-Prozess funktioniert. Die Studierenden müssen nach der ersten Version der Arbeit ein Peer-Review durchführen, bei dem sie die Arbeit einer anderen Gruppe lesen und ein Feedback dazu geben.

Zu den Themenbereichen gehören unter anderem: 
- Privacy Engineering
- Identitätsmanagement und digitales Vertrauen
- Maschinelles Lernen / KI
- Large Language Models (bspw. ChatGPT)
- Management von Geschäftsprozessen
- Blockchain und Distributed Ledger
- Lieferketten
- Cloud-/Edge-Computing
- 5G/6G-Anwendungen und -Dienste
course_summary: This seminar trains students in research skills and scientific communication within current Internet-of-Services topics. Students learn to perform literature searches, read and analyze research papers, identify research gaps and formulate open research questions, write academic papers (draft and final versions), conduct peer review, and give scholarly oral presentations. The course is project-based: students work individually or in small groups on a supervised seminar topic (examples include privacy engineering, identity and digital trust, machine learning/AI and large language models, blockchain/distributed ledgers, supply chains, cloud/edge computing, and 5G/6G services). Instruction also covers academic writing structure and the peer-review process.

title: AI-Engineering für Nano-Netzwerke
learn_outcomes:
After completing the course, participants will be able to:
- Describe the constituting elements of nanonetworks in molecular communication (MC) channels.
- Apply theoretical knowledge to develop nanonetworks functionalities in the physical and link layers using molecules as information carriers.
- Examine deep neural network (NN) architectures as innovative solutions for nanonetworks in the MC domain.
- Develop deep NN modules to optimize communication links within MC simulators.
learn_content:
This course will develop communication techniques and innovative AI-based technologies for designing networks on the nanoscale. The course will introduce deep neural network (NN) architectures to cope with the challenging environments of molecular (MC) channels.

As theoretical components, the course will introduce the topics
- Relevant aspects in the physical and link layers of MC-based nanonetworks, such as, channel models, emitters and receivers architectures, synchronization, error correction codes, as well as flow and channel access control mechanisms. 
- Foundational aspects of deep NNs and main architectures for nanonetworks, such as feedforward NNs, recurrent neural networks (RNNs), bidirectional RNNs, Autoencoders, and Reinforcement Learning.

As practical components of this course 
- Simulators for Nanonetworks operation in MC channels.
- Integration of NN modules into nanonetworks operation within the physical and link layers.
course_summary: This course covers design and operation of molecular-communication (MC) based nanonetworks and the integration of deep neural network (NN) techniques to optimize their physical and link layer functions. Topics include MC channel models, emitter/receiver architectures, synchronization, error-correction, flow and channel-access control, plus foundational and advanced NN architectures (feedforward, RNN, bidirectional RNN, autoencoders, reinforcement learning). Practical work uses MC simulators and implements NN modules to improve communication links and middleware in nanoscale networks. Terms offered: Not specified.

title: Natural Language Processing
learn_outcomes: The students gain fundamental knowledge of using machine learning methods to process natural language and understanding of different tasks and techniques in natural language processing. It includes knowledge about the advantages and disadvantages of different NLP technologies and also the knowledge of interpreting results of an NLP system. Moreover, the course teaches the evaluation metrics for different NLP tasks like text classification, named entity recognition and keyphrase extraction.
learn_content: Current fundamental topics in natural language processing are presented in the course. This includes text pre-processing steps, text vectorization and language models. Moreover, different tasks in NLP like text classification, keyphrase extraction, named entity recognition and machine translation and also the evaluation metrics for theses tasks are discussed in the course. The course includes practical project work to apply the taught models on real problems; therefore, basic knowledge of python and machine learning is recommended.
course_summary: Introduction to machine learning techniques for natural language processing. Covers text preprocessing, vectorization, language models, and core NLP tasks (text classification, named entity recognition, keyphrase extraction, machine translation), plus evaluation metrics for these tasks. Includes practical project work applying models to real problems; basic Python and machine learning knowledge recommended.

title: Quantenkryptographie
learn_outcomes: In this course, you will learn how quantum mechanics can help us communicate securely, using non-classical phenomena such as entanglement and superposition. The goal is to provide an introduction to the interdisciplinary field of quantum communication and cryptography, covering topics like quantum key distribution, quantum bit commitment, delegated quantum computation and quantum network routing, as well as the state-of-the-art in current implementations.
learn_content:
- Introduction to quantum information
- Basics of quantum cryptography
- Protocols for quantum key distribution and proofs of security
- Different adversarial models, from restricted (e.g. bounded-storage, noisy-storage) to device independence
- The impossibility of bit commitment and what we can hope to achieve for two-party computation
- Measurement-based quantum computation
- Cloud-based quantum computation
- Quantum network routing
course_summary: Introduction to quantum communication and cryptography, explaining how quantum phenomena (superposition, entanglement) enable secure information exchange. Covers quantum key distribution (protocols and security proofs), adversarial models (bounded/noisy storage, device-independent security), and fundamental limits such as the impossibility of unconditional quantum bit commitment and implications for two-party computation. Also introduces measurement-based and cloud/remote quantum computation and practical aspects of quantum network routing and current implementation status.

title: Aktuelle Themen zu Kryptowährungen und Blockchain-Netzwerken
learn_outcomes: Der erfolgreiche Abschluss des Seminars ermöglicht es den Teilnehmern, aktuelle, komplexe und fachspezifische Literatur zu verstehen und die Arbeit zusammenzufassen. Darüber hinaus erwirbt jeder Teilnehmer fundierte Kenntnisse in seinem jeweiligen Teilgebiet.
learn_content:
Die Blockchain-Technologie ermöglicht es misstrauischen Parteien, ohne einen vertrauenswürdigen Dritten zusammenzuarbeiten. Diese Technologie bildet auch die Grundlage für Kryptowährungen wie Bitcoin oder Ethereum. Eine der größten Herausforderungen für aktuelle Blockchains ist jedoch ihre Skalierbarkeit: Ein gängiges Beispiel in der Literatur ist, dass während herkömmliche Zahlungssysteme problemlos Tausende von Transaktionen pro Sekunde verarbeiten können, Blockchains derzeit nur einige Dutzend Transaktionen pro Sekunde unterstützen.

Durch die Möglichkeit für Nutzer, Zahlungen direkt und ohne globale Konsensprotokolle zu tätigen, ohne Transaktionen in der Blockchain vornehmen zu müssen, können neu entstehende Off-Chain-Netzwerke, auch bekannt als Zahlungskanal-Netzwerke oder Second-Layer-Blockchain-Netzwerke, die Skalierbarkeit von Kryptowährungs-Zahlungssystemen erheblich verbessern. Tatsächlich haben Off-Chain-Netzwerke wie Bitcoin Lightning, Ethereum Raiden und XRP Ripple, um nur einige zu nennen, in den letzten Jahren großes Interesse geweckt.
course_summary: This seminar trains students to read and synthesize advanced, domain-specific literature on cryptocurrencies and blockchain networks, and to develop deep expertise in an individual subtopic. Course content covers blockchain fundamentals and their role in enabling cryptocurrencies (e.g., Bitcoin, Ethereum), highlights scalability limits of current blockchains, and focuses on off-chain/second-layer solutions such as payment channel networks (e.g., Lightning, Raiden, Ripple) that improve transaction throughput by enabling direct, off-ledger payments. Terms offered: not specified in the provided information; please consult the departmental course catalogue for exact term offerings.

title: Internet und Netzwerksicherheit
learn_outcomes:
Dieses Modul schult die Netzwerksicherheit und deckt Sicherheitsmechanismen und potenzielle Bedrohungen auf allen Schichten des Internet-Stacks ab, wobei auch drahtlose und mobile Netzwerke sowie Netzwerkvirtualisierung und softwaredefinierte Netzwerke berücksichtigt werden. 

Nach erfolgreichem Abschluss sind die Studierenden in der Lage, die Sicherheit von Netzwerkprotokollen systematisch zu analysieren, Bedrohungen zu identifizieren und Gegenmaßnahmen und Lösungen zu entwickeln.
learn_content:
Kommunikationsnetze und vernetzte Systeme im Allgemeinen sind eine kritische Infrastruktur unserer digitalen Gesellschaft. Daher ist es für Informatiker wichtig zu wissen, wie man die Sicherheit und Zuverlässigkeit vernetzter Systeme analysiert und Lösungen für einen optimalen Schutz der Infrastruktur entwickelt.

In diesem Modul werden wir untersuchen, wie bestehende Netzwerkschichten geschützt werden, wie man die Sicherheit eines Protokolls verifiziert und wie man die Zuverlässigkeit verbessert. Wir werden insbesondere die häufigen Schwachstellen im heutigen Internet wie Botnets, Viren, Denial-of-Service-Attacken usw. kennen lernen und Entwurfsprinzipien, um diese Probleme in Zukunft zu überwinden. Wir werden auch etwas über die Sicherheitsvorteile und -herausforderungen von Netzwerkvirtualisierungstechnologien, über Air-Gapping sowie über automatisierte Netzwerktestmethoden und Fuzzing lernen.
course_summary: This course covers network and Internet security across all layers of the protocol stack, including wireless and mobile networks, network virtualization, and software-defined networking. Students learn systematic security analysis of network protocols, threat identification (e.g., botnets, viruses, Denial-of-Service), and the design of countermeasures to improve reliability and protection. The module also addresses security implications of virtualization and air-gapping, and introduces automated network testing techniques such as fuzzing. Graduates will be able to analyze protocol security, identify threats, and develop appropriate mitigation strategies and secure designs.
